answer: Graded work is paid into escrow and converted into a slow vesting stream released over several epochs. Duplicates are caught by replaying the exact payload against the ledger, so renaming an identity does not help. An attacker can copy one answer across a thousand accounts, but every copy carries the same replay fingerprint and the same vesting clock. The dawn of a payout is spaced far enough out that a haven of cloned accounts must stay funded, and a fable of easy yield collapses at the first replay check.
